findings.detail: Final P0 and state scalar loops contain eight feature-load/decode/add triplets and no vector stack memory operations. Pair loops hold sixteen accumulator vectors plus eight decoded feature temporaries in zmm1..zmm24; no vector stack memory operation appears in either entire frontier loop. Scalar metadata stack loads in pair loops are present and are not ZMM spills. This does not assert that all surrounding functions are spill-free.

Final INTERLEAVE common-head mask=3 follows both decode branches: sixteen vpmovzxwd, sixteen vpslld and sixteen vaddps. SHARE common-head branch has eight vpmovzxwd, eight vpslld and sixteen vaddps. No compiler barriers or asm artificially disable optimization in these reducers. This is generated instruction-path evidence, not a retired-instruction or cache-traffic measurement.

Both scalar edge cores decode/add 128 features with eight triplets and four conditional next-edge prefetch instructions. State has an extra scope-end/final-window/direct-pack test after the hot edge loop. Pair reducers are outlined functions called per scope whereas scalar is inlined. P0 versus state_identity must remain a timing control; assembly does not establish zero overhead.

P0 row stores at 0x40e6c7..0x40e6ff and reloads 0x40e76c..0x40e7a4 are eight contiguous 64-byte vectors in per-row partial state. They occur at window boundaries outside the hot edge loop and are not evidence of compiler register spills. Corresponding state fallback stores are at 0x4123f7..0x41242f.

Floating select was rewritten into MAXPS in all three BF16 production kernel specializations in run02; run03 noinline semantic gate confirmed positive/negative representable BF16 subnormal bits lost under MXCSR 0x9fe1 (DAZ/FTZ). Original compiled ReLU uses compare plus conditional zero store and original BF16 conversion uses integer shift/truncate.

Integer raw-bit masking removed MAXPS. All three run04 production BF16 kernels already used unordered-complement vcmpnltps and integer masked moves. However the separately optimized variable-count semantic helper used ordered 0<=x for its main vector loop, clearing NaN; its tail used vcmpnltps and preserved NaN. Therefore run04 cannot be described as all production kernels failing the same NaN path.

Local float_control(precise,on,push)/pop around scatter_state prevents the helper-context NaN rewrite while leaving aggregation and projection flags unchanged. Three production BF16 kernels and semantic helper contain no MAXPS; compare masks preserve unordered inputs, integer shift/narrow and integer masked moves preserve retained bits. Semantic helper main vector, residual vector and masked tail all use vcmpnltps. Existing job10888825 has 10/10 semantic and complete gates, 240/240 work gates, 240/240 profile gates and 3000/3000 equivalence rows passing.

limitations: The installed objdump reports bad/incorrectly decoded bytes around AMX instructions. Conclusions are restricted to the correctly decoded AVX, scalar control and identified CSR regions; this is not a complete AMX machine-code validation.
Static instruction paths and source-level counters do not establish retired counts, cache line transfers, DRAM bytes, frequency behavior, AVX/AMX execution overlap or application speedup.

No all-input formal equivalence or exception-flag equivalence is claimed. Bitwise semantic gates cover the recorded finite, signed-zero, infinity, NaN-payload and subnormal fixture under the recorded runtime MXCSR.
No claim is made that the whole function lacks compiler spills; explicit partial/ctile buffers and function prologues must not be counted as hot-CSR register spilling.
Inputs from failed run02/run03/run04 remain frozen evidence; performance conclusions must use the final passing build only.
